title: Redox and Electrochemistry - Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry - Electrochemistry and Cells
subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: In a galvanic (voltaic) cell, oxidation always occurs at the:
questions.explain: Remember **An Ox** (Anode Oxidation) and **Red Cat** (Reduction Cathode). Oxidation occurs at the anode.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: In a functioning galvanic cell connecting a Zinc electrode and a Copper electrode, which way do electrons flow in the external wire?
questions.explain: Electrons flow from the site of oxidation (Anode) to the site of reduction (Cathode) through the external circuit.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: What is the primary function of the **salt bridge** in an electrochemical cell?
options: To transfer electrons between the solutions
To provide a pathway for ions to maintain electrical neutrality
To increase the voltage of the cell
questions.explain: The salt bridge allows ions to flow between half-cells to balance the charge build-up that would otherwise stop the electron flow. It does not conduct electrons.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q:
Calculate the standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{cell}$) for a cell constructed from the following half-reactions:
$$Zn^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Zn \quad (E^\circ = -0.76\text{ V})$$
$$Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu \quad (E^\circ = +0.34\text{ V})$$
questions.explain:
$E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode}$. Copper has the higher potential, so it is the cathode.
$$E^\circ_{cell} = 0.34 - (-0.76) = 1.10\text{ V}$$
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: Which of the following correctly represents the standard cell notation for a Galvanic cell made of Zinc and Copper?
questions.explain: Standard notation is **Anode | Anode Ion || Cathode Ion | Cathode**. Zinc is oxidized (Anode), Copper is reduced (Cathode).
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q:
Given the standard reduction potentials:
$$Ag^+ + e^- \rightarrow Ag \quad E^\circ = +0.80\text{ V}$$
$$Zn^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Zn \quad E^\circ = -0.76\text{ V}$$
What is the standard potential for the spontaneous reaction between these two couples?
questions.explain:
The spontaneous reaction involves the reduction of the higher potential species (Ag) and oxidation of the lower (Zn).
$$E^\circ_{cell} = E^\circ_{cathode} - E^\circ_{anode} = 0.80 - (-0.76) = 1.56\text{ V}$$
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: The Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE) is assigned a potential of exactly:
questions.explain: By definition, the standard electrode potential of the standard hydrogen electrode (SHE) is exactly **0.00 V**.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q: Which condition indicates that a redox reaction is **spontaneous** under standard conditions?
questions.explain: A positive standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{cell} > 0$) corresponds to a negative Gibbs Free Energy ($\Delta G^\circ < 0$), which indicates spontaneity.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry

questions.q:
Using the table below, which metal can spontaneously reduce $Pb^{2+}$ ions?

| Half-Reaction | $E^\circ$ (V) |
| :--- | :--- |
| $Mg^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Mg$ | -2.37 |
| $Zn^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Zn$ | -0.76 |
| $Pb^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Pb$ | -0.13 |
| $Cu^{2+} + 2e^- \rightarrow Cu$ | +0.34 |
questions.explain: For a metal to reduce $Pb^{2+}$, it must be a stronger reducing agent (have a more negative $E^\circ$) than Pb. Magnesium ($Mg$, -2.37 V) is more negative than Lead ($Pb$, -0.13 V), so Mg can reduce $Pb^{2+}$.
questions.subject: Redox Reactions and Electrochemistry
